The neck is mostly maple or walnut, solid and durable. The strings are gut or metal: the top strings are often gut wound with metal wire and the bass strings plain gut. The pegs and the fittings may be bone, ivory or wood, showing the fineness of the workmanship.
小西奧爾博琴是義大利的罕見弦鳴樂器，屬長頸魯特琴家族，可視為小型西奧爾博琴；琴體: The tiorbino is a rare Italian chordophone of the long-necked lute family, essentially a small tiorba; its body is markedly smaller and it sounds an octave above the tiorba. It appeared at the end of the sixteenth century, and in the seventeenth century continuo players used it, which gave bass accompaniment another colour at the time. It is not loud but carries a long way; it was later lost, and was taken up again at the end of the twentieth century with the early-music revival.
小西奧爾博琴為弦鳴樂器，屬長頸魯特琴家族，外形近似西奧爾博琴但明顯較小，音高較高: The tiorbino is a chordophone of the long-necked lute family, close in shape to the tiorba but clearly smaller and an octave higher. It appeared at the end of the sixteenth century and was in use in the seventeenth, for example in a 1622 work by Bellerofonte Castaldi. It was also used as a figured-bass instrument; it then fell out of use, and was noticed again at the end of the twentieth century through the early-music revival.
小西奧爾博琴的聆聽線索可從十七世紀通奏低音編制尋找。它曾作為通奏低音樂器，音色穿: Clues for listening to the tiorbino come from seventeenth-century continuo writing. It was used as a continuo instrument, with a penetrating timbre that can enrich the continuo sound. One clear surviving example is Bellerofonte Castaldi's 1622 Capricci a due stromenti cioe tiorba e tiorbino e per sonar varie sorti de balli, in which it plays various dances alongside the tiorba. After the early-music revival of the late twentieth century the instrument came back into use.
小西奧爾博琴音色明亮清透，具有獨特的穿透力與靈巧感。由於琴體相對小型，其音調較母: The tiorbino's timbre is bright and clear, with a distinctive penetration and agility. Because the body is relatively small it sounds an octave above its parent instrument the tiorba, and its tone is crisp rather than deep, with an elegant classical flavour. The vibration of the strings produces rich overtones, which give the sound a brilliant sheen. Its range is on the high side, and it is good at fine phrases and ornaments. Because the body is small its resonance is relatively compact, and it is quieter than the tiorba and the lute, but its timbre is more delicate. Compared with the violin of its own time, the tiorbino has a gentler plucked quality; compared with the harp, it has more of the warm character of a string instrument. This distinctive sound gives it a nimble role in Baroque music.
